title: On Approaching the house from the north
subtitle: 决策选择 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）
meta: 主题语境：决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）　|　核心词汇：approach　|　正文 351 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 approach 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1972 the cook ① approached the house from the north with great care, and every guest in the canteen said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the cook ② approaches the house from the north on the same day without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ approach the house from the north at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ approached the house from the north before — a line in the menu for September 1966 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Approaching the house from the north with great care, the cook said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the bowl at the far table, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ approach the trouble at the mill on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Approach the trouble at the mill at once and never mention it again.

By 1979 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the menu, and a new guest from the next canteen ⑧ approaches the trouble at the mill with great care every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the table, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ approached the house from the north again when nobody else would.

⑩ To approach the house from the north, my mother said in 1984, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the canteen remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the canteen forgets, somebody approaches the house from the north on the same day again and somebody must approach the house from the north with great care all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 走近（一般过去式 approached the house from the north：1972 年厨子头一回这样做，小心翼翼地）
B. v. 走近（一般现在 approaches the house from the north：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 走近（不定式 to approach the house from the north：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 走近（过去完成时 had approached the house from the north：1966 年九月的菜单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 走近（动名词 approaching the house from the north 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 着手处理（approach the trouble at the mill：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去着手处理磨坊那边出的麻烦）
G. v. 着手处理（approach the trouble at the mill：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 走近（后段两处：新来的客人照例 approaches the trouble at the mill，而母亲又一次 approached the house from the north）

answers.why: approach 意为“走近”，1972 年厨子小心翼翼地走近从北面走近那座房子，那是食堂里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 approached。
approach 意为“走近”，自那以后厨子当天就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 approaches。
approach 意为“走近”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯走近从北面走近那座房子”，此处为不定式 to approach the house from the north。
approach 意为“走近”，菜单里 九月 那行字说明早在 1979 年之前就有人走近过，故用过去完成时 had approached。
approach 意为“走近”，厨子说“走近从北面走近那座房子这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 approaching the house from the north 作主语。
approach 意为“着手处理”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去着手处理磨坊那边出的麻烦”，should ever 之后用原形 approach the trouble at the mill。
approach 意为“着手处理”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻着手处理磨坊那边出的麻烦（approach the trouble at the mill at once），以后再也不要提起。
approach 意为“走近”，新来的客人每个日子都照例着手处理磨坊那边出的麻烦，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 approaches。
approach 意为“走近”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次小心翼翼地走近从北面走近那座房子，用一般过去式 approached 叙述。
approach 意为“走近”，结尾那句是母亲 1984 年的话：要走近从北面走近那座房子，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和食堂记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 approach 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1972 the cook approached the house from the north with great care, and nobody in the canteen forgot it.
Even now the cook approaches the house from the north on the same day whenever the canteen asks.
Approaching the house from the north with great care, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever approach the trouble at the mill on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new guest from the next canteen approaches the trouble at the mill with great care every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother approached the house from the north again, and the canteen remembered that half.
